title: Sell Mineral Rights in Roseville, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Roseville, PA
metaDescription: Roseville, Tioga County mineral rights owner in the dry-gas Marcellus core? We buy oil and gas interests, explain your lease, and pay cash quickly.
heroLead: Roseville sits in Tioga County, near the New York border in a part of the state that saw some of the most intense leasing activity anywhere during the 2008 to 2010 Marcellus rush, with landmen working farm by farm across the county in a matter of months.
intro: Tioga County families remember that period vividly — leasing agents moving quickly, neighbors comparing bonus offers, and a lot of paperwork signed under real time pressure. If your family's lease near Roseville dates back to that stretch, we can help you understand what it actually says and what your interest is worth today, separate from whatever it seemed like it would be worth at the time.

sections.heading: The 2008-2010 Leasing Rush in Tioga County
paragraphs: Tioga County was one of the counties where per-acre bonus payments climbed fastest during the initial boom, and Roseville-area leases from that window sometimes carry royalty and deduction terms that look dated by today's standards. We read through your actual lease before quoting a number, since the specific language matters more than the general reputation of when it was signed.

Dry-gas Marcellus wells in this part of the state have generally shown strong initial production followed by a steady decline, and we price against where your unit sits on that curve now, not where it was in its first year or two.

sections.heading: What Selling Looks Like From Here
paragraphs: Once we've reviewed your lease and confirmed your fractional interest through the Tioga County recorder of deeds in Wellsboro, we make an offer that reflects current production trends, and if you accept, we handle the transfer paperwork directly with the operator.

faqs.question: My lease is from the original 2008-2010 boom. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It can, since lease terms and deduction language from that era vary widely. We review your specific document rather than assuming based on the date alone.

faqs.question: How is my interest valued if production has declined a lot?
faqs.answer: We price against current production and recent royalty history, which naturally reflects any decline that's already happened.

faqs.question: Do I need to involve the gas company to sell my minerals?
faqs.answer: No, you're selling your ownership interest to us, not renegotiating with the operator. We handle notifying them of the ownership change after closing.

faqs.question: My bonus payment from 2009 was the biggest check I've ever gotten. Should I expect anything close to that now?
faqs.answer: Bonus payments and mineral rights sale prices are different things valued differently, so we'll give you an honest, current number rather than a comparison to that early bonus.
